title: Riemann Surfaces, Branched Maps, and Differentials

items.title: Slab triangulation of a compact plane region bounded by finitely many piecewise real-analytic curves
items.statement: Let R in C be compact and the closure of a bounded connected open set whose boundary is a finite disjoint union of piecewise real-analytic simple closed curves. For every finite P inside R there is a finite union of curvilinear triangles with piecewise Puiseux-analytic rectifiable edges covering R, pairwise interior-disjoint and meeting only in full edges or common vertices, with no point of P on an edge. The construction is choice free.

references.title: Jürgen Jost, Compact Riemann Surfaces, Chapter 2
Guillaume Valette, On subanalytic geometry (2025), Theorem 1.2.3 and Proposition 1.8.4

items.proof_strategy: Choose a direction avoiding finitely many critical heights of the prescribed points; cut by horizontal walls through boundary tangencies and every endpoint of a chosen analytic-piece decomposition, including smooth joins. In each strip the boundary is a finite ordered family of analytic graphs with Puiseux endpoint expansions. Each nonpinched band is pulled back from a rectangle: choose an interior height and a generic fan apex, fan to all existing marks on the top and bottom walls, and obtain graph-bounded triangular cells with rectifiable Puiseux-analytic sides that avoid the prescribed finite set. Treat pinched bands as triangles or cut below their prescribed points first. The fans add no wall marks, so adjacent bands meet face to face. All selections are finite and choice free.

items.title: Index of the boundary of a graph-bounded plane region
items.statement: For a graph-bounded plane region T={w<=y<=w', alpha(y)<=x<=beta(y)} with alpha<=beta continuous, real-analytic on the open interval and Puiseux-analytic rectifiable graphs, the positively oriented boundary contour gamma is a closed complex contour with winding number 1 at every interior point of T and 0 at every point outside T; hence gamma is null-homologous in every open set containing T. The same holds for orientation-preserving similarities of T. The construction and index computations are choice free.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis, Definition 5.24 and the cycle-existence remark

items.proof_strategy: Deform the graph-bounded region by straightening its analytic graph sides into distant vertical lines, transport the boundary contour by an explicit homotopy inside a large disc, and compute the index of a rectangle boundary by the argument increment along its four sides; the outer region contributes index zero by the local constancy and vanishing-at-infinity of the index for cycles. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Riemann surfaces and holomorphic atlases
items.statement: A Riemann surface is a nonempty connected Hausdorff second-countable topological space with charts to open subsets of C whose transition maps in both directions are holomorphic. A compatible covering family of charts extends uniquely to a maximal atlas; connectedness is part of the convention.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.strategy: Define charts and compatibility, check holomorphic transitions compose and invert, and show the maximal compatible atlas is uniquely determined. Nonempty and no-boundary conventions are explicit.

items.title: Local holomorphic charts on nonsingular complex algebraic curves
items.statement: Let C be a complex affine algebraic curve embedded in C^N, or a complex projective algebraic curve embedded in CP^N, that is nonsingular at p in the Jacobian-rank sense. Then a neighborhood of p in C is biholomorphic to a plane domain via one free ambient coordinate in a suitable affine chart. On overlaps, all such local parameters have holomorphic transition maps.
items.proof_strategy: For an affine point, select N−1 local defining polynomials whose differential matrix has rank N−1 and permute coordinates so the Jacobian in the N−1 dependent variables is invertible. The published several-variable holomorphic implicit-function theorem represents the common zero set locally as a holomorphic graph over the remaining coordinate. Nonsingularity and local dimension one ensure these equations describe C near p; explicitly use the local ideal/rank hypothesis rather than infer equality from a subvariety inclusion. The free-coordinate projection and graph map are mutually holomorphic. At a projective point choose a nonzero homogeneous coordinate and dehomogenize; the same argument applies. On chart overlaps, the new free coordinate is a holomorphic function of the old graph parameter, and the inverse is holomorphic by the corresponding graph parameterization.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Chapter 1 §2, Examples 1.9(iii–iv)
Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 5, holomorphic implicit-function theorem

items.title: Holomorphic maps and meromorphic functions on Riemann surfaces
items.statement: A map X→Y between Riemann surfaces is holomorphic when every chart expression is holomorphic. A meromorphic function on X is a holomorphic map X→the Riemann sphere that is not identically infinity; in a finite target chart it is locally a usual meromorphic function, with poles at points sent to infinity.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.strategy: Use holomorphic chart changes and the chain rule to show independence of source and target charts. At a pole use the reciprocal sphere coordinate to prove equivalence with a local meromorphic function; exclude the constant-infinity map.

items.title: Finite chartwise triangulation of a compact Riemann surface
items.statement: For a compact Riemann surface X and finite F⊂X there is an oriented chart cellulation by finitely many chart-contained graph-bounded curvilinear triangle cells with piecewise Puiseux-analytic rectifiable boundaries; a finite common subedge subdivision pairs boundary arcs with opposite orientations, and F lies in cell interiors. The cells admit a finite face-to-face topological triangulation refining them, still chart-contained and avoiding F on edges. The refined edges carry no asserted analytic regularity. No choice axiom is used.

references.title: Jürgen Jost, Compact Riemann Surfaces, Ch. 2 §2.3.A and §2.4.A
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Choose a finite relatively compact round-chart-disc cover and generic boundary circles, forming a finite embedded graph in general position away from F. Each arrangement face has fixed disc membership and closure in one chart. Apply the planar graph-bounded triangulation lemma independently to each face. Collect all cell boundary vertices on each arrangement edge and take their common finite subdivision, giving paired rectifiable subedges with opposite induced orientations. Separately cone from generic interior points of closed-triangle parameter domains to all common boundary marks, obtaining a strict face-to-face topological refinement inside the same charts and avoiding F. All choices are finite.

items.title: Meromorphic differentials, orders and residues
items.statement: A meromorphic differential ω on a Riemann surface is a compatible family of local expressions h(z)dz with meromorphic h and transition law h_w(w)=h_z(z(w))z′(w). For nonzero ω its order at p is the Laurent order of h in a centered chart and its residue is the coefficient of z^(-1)dz; both are chart-independent.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.strategy: Derive the coefficient transition by the chain rule. A coordinate transition has nonzero derivative, so multiplication by that unit preserves the local order. Express the residue as the small positively oriented contour integral divided by 2πi; holomorphic coordinate changes preserve orientation and the change-of-variables integral, proving coefficient invariance. The zero differential has no finite order and residue zero.

items.title: Local power-map normal form on Riemann surfaces
items.statement: For a nonconstant holomorphic map f:X→Y and x∈X, there are source and target holomorphic coordinates centered at x and f(x) in which f is z↦z^e for a unique positive integer e.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: The chart expression cannot be locally constant unless f is globally constant: propagate constancy by the identity theorem across overlapping connected charts. Apply the published planar normal-form theorem to the nonconstant chart expression after centering the target. Shrink source and target to discs on which the resulting coordinate is biholomorphic and verify uniqueness of e as the local zero order.

items.title: Ramification index, ramification order and branch value
items.statement: For a nonconstant holomorphic map f:X→Y, e_x(f) is the unique exponent in its local power-map normal form; e_x−1 is the ramification order. A critical point has e_x>1, and a branch value is its image. The index is independent of all chart choices.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.strategy: Identify e_x with the zero order of a centered target coordinate composed with f. Any other centered target coordinate differs by a holomorphic unit times the first; any source coordinate change has a simple zero, so the order is invariant. Local z^e shows critical points are isolated.

items.title: Residue theorem on a compact Riemann surface
items.statement: For every meromorphic differential on a compact Riemann surface, the finite sum of its residues is zero. This chart-triangulation proof uses no choice axiom and no global de Rham or Stokes theorem.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6
Vladimir Hinich, Riemann Surfaces, lecture 7, §§8.4.3–8.5.3

items.proof_strategy: A nonzero differential has isolated poles, hence finitely many on compact X. Apply the chartwise cellulation lemma with all poles in interiors of its original graph-bounded Puiseux cells. On each cell, use its chart and the plane residue theorem for the positively oriented rectifiable boundary; the graph-bounded index lemma gives index one at interior poles and zero outside. Sum the identities and split every boundary contour at the common finite subedge vertices. Each subedge integral appears exactly twice with opposite orientation, so the total is zero. Treat the zero differential separately; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Pullback order formula for a branched holomorphic map
items.statement: If f:X→Y is nonconstant holomorphic, x∈X, y=f(x), e=e_x(f), and η is a nonzero meromorphic differential near y, then ord_x(f*η)=e·ord_y(η)+e−1. This is the local analytic Riemann–Hurwitz interface; it makes no global canonical-divisor existence claim.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Use coordinates with w=z^e. Write η=w^k u(w)dw with u(0)≠0 and k∈Z. Pullback is e z^(e(k+1)−1)u(z^e)dz, whose unit coefficient gives the stated order. Check chart independence through the differential and index definitions. No Riemann–Roch or nonzero global meromorphic differential is assumed.

items.title: Degree of a proper holomorphic map of Riemann surfaces
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be nonconstant holomorphic between connected Riemann surfaces and proper (preimages of compact sets are compact). Then f is onto, every fibre is finite, the branch values are locally finite, and d=Σ_{x∈f^(-1)(y)}e_x is one positive finite integer independent of y. Off the branch values f is a finite-sheeted covering of degree d.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Local z^e makes f open and each fibre discrete. Properness and a compact target chart disc make each fibre compact, hence finite. To show closedness, for y outside the image of a closed C take a compact closed chart disc K about y; the compact set C∩f^(-1)(K) has compact closed image, so a smaller target neighborhood misses f(C). The nonempty open-and-closed image is all connected Y. For each fibre choose disjoint normal-form neighborhoods around its finitely many points; remove the closed image of the remaining points over a compact target disc to find one neighborhood with no extra preimages. Nearby regular fibres then have Σe_x points. At a branch value, the local model counts e_x with multiplicity; connectedness propagates the integer. Properness also makes the image of the closed discrete critical set locally finite. Over the complement, the same finite-neighborhood construction gives evenly covered discs.

items.title: Topological classification of compact Riemann surfaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The holomorphic atlas canonically orients every compact Riemann surface. A finite chart triangulation and polygonal reduction identify it with S² with a unique number g≥0 of handles.

references.title: Jürgen Jost, Compact Riemann Surfaces, Ch. 2 §2.3.A and §2.4.A
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: In each chart use the standard orientation of C; a holomorphic transition has real Jacobian |φ′|²>0 and therefore preserves it. Feed the finite chart triangulation to the in-run compact-surface classification theorem, whose polygonal normal-form proof reduces the oriented triangulation to the empty reduced word (the sphere digon is the geometric schema) or g commutator blocks. The nonorientable square-word branch is excluded by the complex orientation. Uniqueness comes from the classification theorem’s orientation and Euler-characteristic invariant. AC is used exactly through that in-run classification theorem, whose topological finite-triangulation/Schoenflies chain assumes it; the chart orientation and local triangulation themselves add no choice.

items.title: Genus and Euler characteristic of a compact Riemann surface
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The genus g(X) of a compact Riemann surface is its unique handle count from topological classification, and its Euler characteristic, computed from any finite triangulation or polygonal schema, is χ(X)=2−2g(X). Both are independent of the holomorphic atlas and chosen triangulation.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6
Jürgen Jost, Compact Riemann Surfaces, Ch. 2 §2.3.A and §2.4.A

items.strategy: Use the oriented classification theorem and the in-run orientable Euler-characteristic corollary. Count one face, 2g edges and one vertex in the g-commutator polygon (sphere is the empty-word case), giving 2−2g. The supplier proves homeomorphism invariance, so chart and triangulation choices do not change the number. AC is inherited exactly from classification, not from the finite cell count.

items.title: Riemann–Hurwitz formula for compact Riemann surfaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a nonconstant holomorphic map f:X→Y of compact connected Riemann surfaces and degree d, 2g(X)−2=d(2g(Y)−2)+Σ_{x∈X}(e_x−1). The ramification sum is finite. The local analytic pullback-order formula and this Euler-characteristic cell count are the two interfaces; the proof does not assume a global canonical differential.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6
Vladimir Hinich, Riemann Surfaces, lecture 7, §§8.4.3–8.5.3

items.proof_strategy: Compactness makes f proper, and the degree theorem makes the critical/branch set finite. Choose the face-to-face topological refinement of the chart cellulation of Y. Insert every branch value into a face, then subdivide every edge once so no triangle has two branch-value vertices. Pull it back off those vertices. Each open edge and face has d unramified lifts; triviality of a connected covering over a contractible cell and the local z^e model show lifted closures form a finite cell decomposition of X. Above a target vertex y, the number of lifted vertices is d−Σ_{x|y}(e_x−1), because Σ_{x|y}e_x=d. Hence E_X=dE_Y, F_X=dF_Y and V_X=dV_Y−Σ_x(e_x−1); subtract to get χ(X)=dχ(Y)−Σ(e_x−1), then substitute χ=2−2g. Separately cite the immediately preceding local analytic pullback-order lemma, rather than deriving the global formula from a canonical divisor whose existence is not yet known. AC enters only through the genus/classification interface.

title: Riemann Surfaces, Branched Maps, and Differentials: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Atlases on the sphere, plane, disc and annulus
items.statement: The standard sphere charts z and 1/z, and the single identity charts on C, the unit disc and every round annulus, satisfy the Riemann-surface axioms; the sphere chart transition is 1/z on C*.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Check the sphere’s two chart domains cover and have holomorphic reciprocal transition. Each open connected plane domain has one identity chart and inherits Hausdorffness and a countable rational-disc basis. Include the punctured-plane/annulus boundary conventions explicitly.

items.title: The complex torus as a Riemann surface
items.statement: For a full lattice Λ=Zω₁+Zω₂ in C with Im(ω₂/ω₁)>0, C/Λ is a compact Riemann surface. Small-disc quotient charts have transition functions z↦z+λ for λ∈Λ.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: The lattice has a positive shortest nonzero-vector bound, so projection is injective on discs of radius below half that bound. Quotient openness gives charts, and on a connected overlap the lifts differ by one fixed lattice translation; on a disconnected overlap check each component. A closed fundamental parallelogram surjects onto the quotient, proving compactness. Use translated small discs to separate distinct orbits and a countable rational-disc cover to prove Hausdorffness and second countability.

items.title: A nonsingular affine conic is a punctured-plane Riemann surface
items.statement: The affine algebraic curve x²+y²=1 in C² is nonsingular and is biholomorphic to C* via u=x+iy, with inverse x=(u+u^(-1))/2 and y=(u−u^(-1))/(2i).

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Factor (x+iy)(x−iy)=1, so u is nonzero and the displayed inverse lies on the curve. The two formulas are holomorphic and inverse; transfer the C* atlas. The gradient (2x,2y) cannot vanish on the equation, checking nonsingularity directly without importing a later holomorphic implicit-function theorem.

items.title: Nonsingular affine and projective curves as Riemann surfaces
items.statement: Every nonsingular complex affine or projective algebraic curve, component by component, has the Riemann-surface atlas supplied by local ambient-coordinate graphs. A projective curve is compact in its analytic topology. The nonsingular conic x²+y²=1 is an explicit affine instance.
items.proof_strategy: Apply the local chart lemma at every point. The affine and projective ambient spaces are Hausdorff and second countable (finitely many affine projective charts), so each connected component with the graph atlas satisfies the Riemann-surface convention; algebraic curves have finitely many components, and components are open for a nonsingular one-dimensional variety. For compactness of a projective curve, the unit sphere S^(2N+1) is compact by Heine–Borel, the coordinate-line quotient map onto CP^N is continuous and surjective, and CP^N is compact. The projective zero locus is closed, so it is compact. The separate explicit conic example computes the concrete punctured-plane parameter.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Chapter 1 §2, Examples 1.9(iii–iv)
Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, Chapter 5, holomorphic implicit-function theorem

items.title: Orders and residues under inversion on the sphere
items.statement: On the Riemann sphere, ω=dz/z has simple poles at 0 and infinity with residues +1 and −1; dz has order −2 and residue 0 at infinity. These computations agree with the compact residue theorem.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: In the infinity coordinate w=1/z calculate dz/z=−dw/w and dz=−dw/w². Read orders and z^(-1) coefficients in both charts; note dz/z has no other poles, so the residues cancel. This also checks the transition law rather than treating infinity as an ordinary finite coordinate.

items.title: The exponential map has no finite proper-map degree
items.statement: The holomorphic local biholomorphism exp:C→C* is not proper: exp^(-1)({1})=2πiZ is infinite and noncompact. Thus local biholomorphism alone does not imply a finite-sheeted proper covering or a finite degree.

references.title: Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: The derivative exp is nowhere zero, so local inverse charts apply. The published exponential-fibre formula identifies the fibre of 1 as 2πiZ, an unbounded closed discrete set; {1} is compact. Its inverse image is not compact, violating properness. Contrast explicitly with the degree theorem’s proper hypothesis.

items.title: Hyperelliptic double covers and their genus
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a squarefree polynomial P(x)=∏_{j=1}^m(x−a_j) with m=2g+1 or 2g+2 and g≥1, the affine curve y²=P(x), completed by the explicit infinity charts below, is a connected compact Riemann surface with a degree-two map to the sphere. The m finite roots are simple branch values; infinity is branched exactly when m is odd. Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus g.

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6

items.proof_strategy: Over a finite x away from roots, use the published local holomorphic-logarithm lemma to choose a square root of P and take the two graph sheets; continuation around a simple root exchanges them. Near a_j write P=(x−a_j)u(x) with u(a_j)≠0, take a local root of u and coordinate s=y/sqrt(u(x)), obtaining x−a_j=s² and one point of index two; the inverse chart is x=a_j+s², y=s sqrt(u(a_j+s²)). At infinity set t=1/x and v=y t^(g+1). If m=2g+2, v²=∏(1−a_j t), giving two holomorphic branches v=±sqrt(product) over t=0 and no ramification. If m=2g+1, v²=t∏(1−a_j t); absorb the nonzero factor into a coordinate s so t=s², giving one point of index two. Glue the finite and infinity charts along their explicit algebraic transitions. For sufficiently large R, the part with |x|≤R is a closed subset of a bounded subset of C² because |y|²=|P(x)| is bounded, hence compact by Heine–Borel; the complement is contained in finitely many small closed infinity-chart discs. These compact pieces cover the completed surface, proving compactness and properness of its sphere projection. Monodromy around any simple root exchanges the two sheets, giving connectedness. The total ramification is m for even m and m+1 for odd m, always 2g+2; insert d=2 and g_Y=0 in Riemann–Hurwitz to obtain g_X=g. AC is inherited from Riemann–Hurwitz only; the chart construction uses finite choices.

items.title: Riemann–Hurwitz for the sphere power map
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The map z↦z^n on the Riemann sphere (n≥1) has degree n, indices n at 0 and infinity and index 1 elsewhere; Riemann–Hurwitz reads −2=−2n+2(n−1).

references.title: Eduard Looijenga, Riemann Surfaces (2007), Ch. 1 §2, Ch. 4 §§2–3, Ch. 6 §2
Curtis T. McMullen, Riemann Surfaces, Math 213b course notes (2026), Chs. 2–3 and 6
Vladimir Hinich, Riemann Surfaces, lecture 7, §§8.4.3–8.5.3

items.proof_strategy: At 0 the local expression is z^n. At infinity with w=1/z and v=1/f(z), it is v=w^n. A nonzero finite value has n distinct roots, so the degree is n. The sphere has genus zero by the classified model; substitute the two ramification contributions n−1. AC is inherited only from the genus/Riemann–Hurwitz interface; the local map computation is choice-free.
